quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: Section 10(a) gives us a broad Kubient defend-and-indemnify obligation for third-party Claims arising out of or in connection with the Services, the Auction Platform, the Creative, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. Because Kubient's warranties in Section 9(b) expressly include non-infringement of third-party IP (9(b)(i), (vii), (viii)), compliance with applicable Law (9(b)(v), (ix)) and secure handling of data (9(b)(iii)), the indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement claims, breach of law, data security failures and Kubient's own misconduct — meeting the preferred position, with no IP carve-out and no super-cap or aggregate liability cap limiting it (Section 7 preserves indemnification liability from the consequential-damages waiver). Section 11 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a forfeiture, indemnitor control of defence with consent required for liability-admitting settlements, cooperation at the indemnitor's cost). Our reciprocal indemnity in Section 10(b) is confined to our own Content and Properties, our own breaches and our own acts or omissions rather than Kubient's Services; the references to our "unauthorized or inappropriate use" and acts/omissions are marginally wider than the preferred narrow formulation, which we note but do not redline as it does not shift indemnity for the Services onto us.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
rationale: Paragraph (h) gives AP the affiliate/successor carve-out we require: it may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. The termination provisions (p0016) contain no change-of-control trigger and no re-pricing right for Kubient on AP's change of control, so the walk-away scenarios are absent. The clause is mutual rather than one-way, so it sits at the playbook fallback (mutual right to assign to successors, consent otherwise not unreasonably withheld); the only shortfalls of the preferred position are minor sub-elements — no express bar on assignment to an AP competitor and no written-notice mechanic — which we note but do not redline.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: The Services clause (Section 1) expressly disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms that AP remains free to offer Inventory via other agents or sell it to third parties, so AP's freedom to use other vendors is fully preserved. The only other "exclusive" references are the non-exclusive license grant to us (p0002), exclusive jurisdiction (p0064), each party's own trademark ownership (p0065) and no-third-party-beneficiary language (p0073) — none imposes a sole-supplier or requirements obligation on AP. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer); no redline required.

quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee obligation payable by AP. Commercially, the deal is a pure revenue share (para. 5): Kubient contracts with Advertisers and remits AP's share within seven days of receipt, so AP owes no subscription or committed fees that could be accelerated on termination. The only termination-related money provision (para. 4(a)) entitles Kubient to fees actually generated during the 90-day notice period — that is earned revenue share on real Impressions, not a liquidated amount or penalty payable by AP, and it drops away entirely where AP terminates for Kubient's material breach. Para. 7(a) also excludes punitive and similar damages for both Parties. Search for "liquidated damages", "penalt", "minimum", "shall pay" and "damages" returned no Customer-payable liquidated sum. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer); no redline required.

quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
rationale: This clause sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. (1) Customer convenience right: AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' written notice, which is within the fallback's 60–90 day band. The suspension of convenience termination during the Initial Term does not trigger the "missing behaviour" deviation because the Initial Term is exactly one (1) year, not longer than 12 months, and renewals are 1-year (not multi-year) periods, so this is not walk-away territory. (2) No early-termination penalty: there is no termination fee or acceleration of future fees; Kubient is entitled only to fees actually "generated during the termination period," i.e., revenue earned for services rendered during the 90-day notice window, well inside the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap. (3) Vendor convenience right: Kubient's mirror right requires ninety (90) days' notice and cannot be exercised during the Initial Term, so it is above the walk-away threshold of "fewer than 90 days." Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position but are noted rather than flagged: Kubient's right runs at any time after the Initial Term rather than only at the end of a term, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund mechanic. The refund point is immaterial here because Section 5 is a revenue-share arrangement (Kubient remits a share of auction revenue to AP) rather than a prepaid subscription, so AP has no prepaid fees at risk. Because the clause meets the fallback on every material term — notice length, absence of penalty, and Vendor notice period — no redline is proposed.

quote: 5. Fees and Payment. The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit.
rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verif" and "records" return nothing, and a full read of the Agreement confirms Kubient has no right to audit, inspect or verify AP's usage, books or records, and no right of access to AP systems. The fees/revenue-share provision (§5) imposes only payment and reporting mechanics running from Kubient to AP, and the use-of-service provision (§6(a)) contains compliance covenants but no inspection right. Because there is no audit right binding us, there is nothing to constrain on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access — the outcome is better than the preferred position, so no redline is warranted. If Kubient later proposes an audit right, we would hold it to no more than once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Kubient's cost absent underpayment above 5%, and with no direct access to AP systems.

quote: (a) This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
rationale: Section 14(a) selects Delaware law, which sits squarely at the playbook fallback (Delaware, California, or England and Wales), and vests exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the state and federal courts located in New York, New York — the preferred forum. No walk-away trigger is present: the law chosen is on the accepted list and the forum is US courts in our preferred county, not Kubient's home jurisdiction or a foreign venue. Section 8's arbitration provision is administered by the AAA under its Commercial Arbitration Rules with no seat outside the United States, so there is no mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Two sub-elements worth noting without flagging: (i) the law/forum split (Delaware substantive law applied by New York courts) is short of the fully preferred New York-law-plus-New-York-courts pairing, and (ii) Section 8's arbitration mandate sits in tension with Section 14(a)'s exclusive court jurisdiction, which could invite a forum dispute. Neither is a material failure of the fallback, so no redline is proposed; we can raise the law/forum alignment as a drafting tidy-up if the negotiation is otherwise open.

ops.text: (b) Ownership of Content, Data and Deliverables. As between the Parties, Customer owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to the Content, the Properties, the Requests and all other data and information provided by, collected from or generated on behalf of Customer, its users or the Properties (collectively, "Customer Data"), together with all deliverables and work product created for Customer under this Agreement or any Exhibit, and Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in and to such deliverables and work product. Kubient retains all right, title and interest in the Auction Platform and its pre-existing and generally applicable technology, tools and know-how, and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any Kubient materials embedded in such deliverables for Customer's business purposes. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Kubient any ownership interest in Customer Data or any other Customer intellectual property, no deliverable or Customer Data shall be jointly owned, and Kubient may use Customer Data solely as necessary to provide the Services.

rationale: The Agreement has no intellectual property or data ownership article. Section 6(a) (p0025) allocates liability for the Content and Properties to us but says nothing about ownership; section 14(b) (p0065) covers only names, trademarks and logos; and Kubient's warranties at p0039-p0040 address only Kubient's own rights in the Service and Auction Platform. There is no assignment of our IP to Kubient (so no walk-away issue), but neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met because no usable ownership/licence clause exists. proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after expiry or termination, and certified deletion into section 4(c)

rationale: Section 4(c) sets out the only effects of termination: Kubient ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, Customer stops using the platform, and each Party returns or destroys the other's Confidential Information. There is no transition or wind-down assistance and no obligation to return or export Customer's Content, Requests or other data in a usable format, nor any certified-deletion timing — a search for transition/exit/export/migration language returns nothing elsewhere in the Agreement. For a hosted auction-platform service this omission fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days), and the bare "return or destroy" of Confidential Information leaves Kubient free to destroy our data on termination, which is walk-away territory. Redline inserts the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter) as new sub-clauses (v)-(vii) of section 4(c); the 90-day fallback is offered in the comment.
